title: Credit Controller
description:
Credit Controller; Wolverhampton; 6 Months; £18 00ph paye; inside IR35
We are currently recruiting for an experienced credit controller to work with an Aerospace and defence sector client based in Wolverhampton. The role will operate on a hybrid working pattern with 3 days on sire required.
This role will have a dual purpose, and be focussed on 2 elements, Credit Control and Accounts Receivable, of which the main aims are.
Credit Control: the main responsibility of the role is to help manage customer credit accounts, minimise bad debt exposure, ensure timely collection of outstanding invoices by working with key internal stakeholders to resolve queries, and maintain healthy cash flow. The role involves assessing credit risk, managing customer relationships, and implementing effective debt collection strategies while maintaining positive customer relationships.
Accounts Receivable: the second element of the role is to assist for maintaining accurate customer accounts, reconciling customer balances, and supporting the efficient collection of outstanding debts. The role ensures that company cash flow is supported through timely and accurate accounts receivable administration. In addition, the reporting of weekly overdue debt status to management
Key Responsibilities of the role
CREDIT CONTROL:
Credit Control and Collections
Monitor aged debtor balances and overdue accounts.
Proactively partner with internal Project Managers and other key stakeholders to secure payment of outstanding invoices.
Issue payment reminders, collection letters, and statements.
Proactively chase customers before and after overdue.
Escalate unresolved debts to the business in accordance with company procedures.
Credit Risk Management
Assess new customer credit applications.
Conduct credit checks and analyse financial information.
Recommend appropriate credit limits and payment terms.
Monitor customer creditworthiness and adjust limits where necessary.
Account Management
Creation of and suppression of customer accounts in ERP and workflows.
With liaison with the business processes and changes in customer data in the ERP and workflows.
Investigate and work with the Project Managers to resolve payment disputes and account queries.
Build and maintain strong relationships with customers.
Negotiate payment plans where appropriate, in agreement with the business.
Reporting
Produce aged debt reports and collection performance reports.
Responsible for statistical provision of Aged/doubtful debt.
Provide regular updates to management on debt recovery activities.
Monitor and report on key credit control metrics.
Compliance and Process Improvement
Ensure compliance with company credit policies.
Support the development of credit control procedures.
Assist with bad debt provisioning and audit requirements.
ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE:
Accounts Receivable Processing
Provide an effective AR service
Maintain customer account records and master data.
Monitor customer account activity and outstanding balances.
Cash Allocation
Support the shared service centre to record and allocate customer payments accurately to retrieving remittance advices from customers.
Manage the release of Cash in Advance customers.
Investigate and resolve unallocated cash receipts.
Reconcile customer accounts and statements.
Account Reconciliation
Perform regular customer account reconciliations.
Investigate discrepancies and work with the Project Managers to resolve billing queries.
Prepare customer statements and account reports.
Customer Service
Respond to customer enquiries regarding invoices, payments, and account balances.
Liaise with the Business to resolve invoice disputes.
Ensure the Business has the required support and maintain robust communications.
Reporting and Compliance
Assist with month-end accounts receivable reconciliation and reporting.
Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation.
Ensure compliance with company policies and accounting procedures.
Comply with all legal and audit requirements.
Additional Role information
Attend meetings as required.
Adhere to all Group policies and procedures.
Take care of your own safety and the safety of others at all times by complying with the HSE policy and procedures.
Travel Specificity
Some travel across UK sites may be required on an ad hoc basis, or as business needs require.
Skills and Competencies
Technical Skills
Strong understanding of accounts receivable, credit control and debt collection processes and practices.
Knowledge of credit risk assessment.
Financial analysis and reconciliation skills.
Proficiency in accounting and ERP systems.
Strong Microsoft Excel skills.
Behavioural Competencies
Excellent negotiation and influencing skills.
Strong organisational, communication and interpersonal skills.
Commercial awareness.
Resilience and persistence.
Ability to work to deadlines.
Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
Sense of responsibility.
Qualifications and Experience
Essential
Previous experience in credit control, collections, or accounts receivable.
Strong understanding of credit management principles.
Experience managing customer accounts and debt recovery activities.

Morson is acting as an employment business in relation to this vacancy.

title: Assistant Company Secretary
description:
Assistant Company Secretary & Compliance Coordinator

Are you a highly organised, detail-focused professional looking to develop your career within corporate governance, compliance, and company secretarial support?

Our client is a large, international organisation operating across multiple sectors, committed to maintaining the highest standards of governance, compliance, and corporate responsibility. They are seeking an Assistant Company Secretary & Compliance Coordinator to join their supportive and collaborative team.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with company secretarial, governance, compliance, risk, GDPR, or corporate administration experience who is looking to take the next step in their career and gain exposure to senior stakeholders, board-level processes, and corporate governance activities.

The Opportunity

Reporting to the Company Secretary, you will play a key role in supporting the governance and compliance activities across a portfolio of UK and Ireland entities. This varied position offers exposure to board administration, statutory compliance, corporate governance, data management, and stakeholder engagement.

Key Responsibilities
- Providing administrative and governance support to the Company Secretary
- Maintaining statutory company records, registers, and regulatory filings
- Preparing and coordinating board and shareholder documentation, including minutes and resolutions
- Managing corporate governance records and company data systems
- Supporting compliance projects and governance initiatives across the business
- Monitoring governance policies and compliance requirements
- Assisting with share-related administration and company structure updates
- Reviewing and managing commercial agreements and documentation
- Supporting board meetings and senior stakeholder communications
- Responding to governance and compliance-related queries from the wider business
- Maintaining accurate electronic records and document management systems
- Supporting data protection and broader compliance activities

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience in a company secretarial, governance, compliance, risk, corporate administration, or similar position
- Strong organisational skills with excellent attention to detail
- Confident written communication skills and experience producing accurate documentation
- Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines
- Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Word, Excel and Outlook
- A proactive and professional approach with the confidence to liaise with senior stakeholders
- High levels of integrity and discretion when handling confidential information
- Experience working within a regulated, corporate, professional services, financial services, insurance, property, or large organisational environment would be advantageous

What's on Offer?
- Hybrid working (typically 2 days in the office)
- Flexible working hours
- Enhanced annual leave entitlement
- Pension scheme
- Life assurance
- Healthcare cash plan
- Enhanced family-friendly policies
- Employee Assistance Programme
- Health and wellbeing initiatives
- Long service awards and recognition programmes
- Genuine long-term career development opportunities

title: Accounts Receivable/Credit Control Administrator
company: MET Recruitment UK Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Accounts Receivable/Credit Control Administrator

Location: Dudley, West Midlands
Salary: Circa £30,000 depending on experience
Job Type: Permanent, Full-time
Working Pattern: Fully office-based

The Opportunity

MET Recruitment is recruiting for an experienced Accounts Receivable Administrator to join an established manufacturing business based in Dudley.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone with a strong background in accounts receivable who enjoys taking ownership of their work, understands the full sales ledger process and takes pride in maintaining accurate financial records.

We're particularly interested in candidates who have gained substantial, hands-on experience within an accounts receivable function and can demonstrate a thorough understanding of the processes involved, rather than simply processing transactions.

The business has recently implemented SAP, so we're looking for someone who is confident working with accounting systems, enjoys problem-solving and can adapt to new processes and the challenges that naturally come with a system implementation.

Key Responsibilities
- Manage day-to-day accounts receivable activities, ensuring transactions are processed accurately and efficiently.
- Raise and process sales invoices, ensuring accurate pricing, VAT treatment and customer information.
- Maintain customer accounts and ensure sales ledger records are accurate and up to date.
- Allocate customer receipts and investigate any discrepancies or unallocated payments.
- Perform customer account and trade debtor reconciliations.
- Monitor outstanding balances, prepare aged debtor reports and support credit control activities.
- Investigate and resolve invoice queries, payment discrepancies and customer account issues.
- Process credit notes, refunds and adjustments where required.
- Support month-end procedures, including reconciliations, revenue cut-off and reporting.
- Work closely with colleagues across Finance, Sales and Operations to resolve queries.
- Assist with identifying and resolving transactional issues as the recently implemented SAP system continues to bed in.
- Maintain accurate financial records and support internal controls and audit requirements.

About You

We're looking for someone who has developed a strong foundation in accounts receivable through substantial practical experience.

You'll ideally have:
- Proven experience within an accounts receivable or sales ledger position, with exposure to the full AR process.
- A stable employment background, demonstrating depth of experience and ownership of responsibilities.
- A sound understanding of double-entry bookkeeping and how sales ledger transactions impact the wider accounts.
- Strong reconciliation skills, with the ability to investigate and resolve discrepancies independently.
- Experience of cash allocation, invoicing, credit control and month-end processes.
- Confidence using accounting systems or ERP software; SAP experience would be advantageous.
- Good Excel skills and a methodical, accurate approach to your work.
- The ability to identify problems, investigate their causes and work towards practical solutions.
- Strong organisational skills and the confidence to manage competing priorities.
- A proactive, inquisitive approach and a genuine interest in understanding how accounting processes work.

Candidates who are currently studying towards AAT, or who have developed equivalent knowledge through practical experience, are particularly welcome.

Experience within a manufacturing or distribution environment would be beneficial but is not essential.

Why Apply?

This is an opportunity to join an established business where you'll play an important role within the finance function.

You'll have the chance to use your existing accounts receivable knowledge, contribute to the smooth running of the sales ledger and support the business as it continues to develop its financial systems and processes.

Salary: Circa £30,000 depending on experience

Please note: This is a fully on-site position based in Dudley, with no hybrid working arrangement.

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk
description:
Purchase Ledger Clerk (Part-Time)

Dudley

25-30 hours per week

£13.50 - £14.00 per hour (dependent on experience)

Temporary to Permanent

Are you an experienced Purchase Ledger professional who enjoys keeping things organised, building great supplier relationships, and making sure every detail is accurate?

We're working with a reputable client in Dudley who are looking for a Purchase Ledger Clerk to join their finance team.

This is a varied role where you'll play a key part in keeping the purchase ledger running smoothly, working closely with suppliers and internal departments to ensure invoices are processed accurately and payments are made on time.

What You'll Be Doing
- Processing and recording supplier invoices accurately and efficiently.
- Matching invoices against purchase orders and goods received notes (GRNs).
- Investigating and resolving invoice, pricing and quantity discrepancies.
- Processing supplier credit notes and reconciling supplier statements.
- Managing supplier accounts and responding to payment and invoice queries.
- Assisting with supplier payment runs and ensuring agreed payment terms are met.
- Working closely with Purchasing, Warehouse and Finance teams to resolve account issues.
- Supporting month-end processes, reconciliations and reporting requirements.
- Maintaining accurate electronic records and audit trails.
- Submitting monthly utility meter readings and providing general finance support when required.

What We're Looking For
- Previous experience within a Purchase Ledger, Accounts Payable or similar finance role.
- Strong attention to detail and a methodical approach to work.
- Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Confident problem-solver who enjoys investigating and resolving discrepancies.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications.
- Strong communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with suppliers and colleagues.
- Experience using accounting or ERP systems would be advantageous.
- Understanding of basic accounting principles and VAT processes is beneficial.

title: Accounts Assistant - Sage Experienced
description:
An outstanding opportunity has arisen for a versatile and motivated Accounts Assistant to join a highly successful, fast-moving manufacturing and food production business located in the Smethwick. Operating within a structured and high-volume finance department, this position is ideal for a well-rounded transactional professional who thrives in a dynamic environment and enjoys taking ownership of a varied workload.

Reporting directly to the Accounts Manager, you will play a pivotal role in supporting the daily operations of the transactional finance function. Your day-to-day responsibilities will involve balancing both sides of the ledger, managing the accurate input and processing of high-volume supplier invoices, and matching delivery notes within a fast-moving supply chain. Additionally, you will take responsibility for daily cash allocation, raising sales invoices for corporate distribution clients, resolving supplier and customer ledger queries efficiently, and assisting with essential bank reconciliations to support the wider team during busy month-end periods.

Skills Required:
- A solid, proven track record operating as an Accounts Assistant or Transactional Finance Assistant, ideally within a manufacturing, distribution, or FMCG environment.
- Good foundational knowledge of both accounts payable and accounts receivable processes.
- Strong IT literacy, including intermediate Microsoft Excel skills and a high level of data entry accuracy and hands-on, practical experience utilising Sage accounting software to manage day-to-day ledger transactions.
- A proactive approach with the ability to communicate confidently across internal production, logistics, and finance teams.

What You Will Receive:
- A stable contract position offering a reliable weekly pay structure and holiday entitlement from day one.
- Free on-site parking alongside convenient access to local transport links.
- Exposure to a fast-paced, commercially successful sector that significantly enhances your interim CV.
- Genuine potential for contract extension or transition into permanent opportunities for the right candidate.

If you are a driven accounts professional looking for a rewarding interim challenge within a stable, forward-thinking industry, we would be delighted to hear from you. This is an excellent opportunity to make an immediate, tangible impact within a supportive finance division that truly values teamwork and individual commitment. To be considered for this immediate-start contract assignment, please submit your up-to-date CV today.
